subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu group isolation be solved with sender/topic-scoped sessions plus memory namespaces, automatic per-user group subagents, or a Feishu plugin experiment before adding SDK/core contracts?
rationale: The request crosses product, security, plugin API, memory isolation, admin authority, lifecycle, cost, and message-routing boundaries that source inspection cannot safely choose automatically.

options.title: Design Feishu Isolation Contract First
options.body: Define sender/topic session semantics, shared/private memory, lifecycle/TTL/quota/admin controls, and live Feishu proof before implementation.

options.title: Prototype In Feishu Plugin
options.body: Keep broad orchestration out of core initially and validate it as a Feishu-owned plugin experiment against real group chats.

options.title: Defer Broad Subagents
options.body: Leave this tracker open while pursuing narrower session identity, threading policy, and user skill preference issues separately.

recommendation.title: Design Feishu Isolation Contract First
recommendation.body: Define sender/topic session semantics, shared/private memory, lifecycle/TTL/quota/admin controls, and live Feishu proof before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest documented Feishu plugin owner signal and are already pulled into the issue timeline for this area.
